## [0.0.2] - 2026-11-13

### Added

- The `jelly` settings declare their choices: `access` is drawn as Allowed, Ask before changes or Read only, with
  Jelly's own line for each (needs a jelly that includes app#1301).

### Known limits

- **No PDF output, and no Plotly or Mermaid input.** [docs/status.md](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/opencode-charts/blob/HEAD/docs/status.md) says what does not work and why, and `charts_capabilities` reports what this build supports.
- **Bundled fonts cover Latin, Greek and Cyrillic.** A label beyond them gets `FONT_GLYPH_MISSING`; the fix is a font file with `theme.font.files`.
- **Built-in themes are neutral.** Brand themes are not in the plugin. Save one with `charts_theme_save`, or set it in the plugin's options, and use it by name.
- **Nothing is loaded from the network.** A remote data file or image is not fetched.
- **Recipes cover the 14 standard types.** The other 39 catalogue types are raw specs; an engine document keeps its
  native layout (no outer-size fitting or responsive reflow) and its own interaction syntax.
- **Four interaction presets.** Tooltip, legend highlight, temporal x zoom and scatter/bubble brush, in the documented
  combinations; no series hiding, no ECharts zoom or brush, and SVG/PNG always show the initial view.
- **PNG and HTML need the packaged runtime.** A missing runtime is reported as `PNG_UNAVAILABLE` or `HTML_UNAVAILABLE`; reinstalling the plugin restores it.
- **Some catalogue examples and the light ramp have rough edges.** The candlestick example's date labels, close-set
  ticks in the histogram and binned heatmap examples, and treemap labels cut short in small cells; the light theme's
  sequential ramp starts near white, so the lowest values in a light heatmap or choropleth sit close to the canvas.
- **Package size.** The package is about 8 MB unpacked, and `dist/index.js` is 2.3 MB: Vega, ECharts and the PNG rasteriser are bundled, so a render needs no network.
- **Host range.** OpenCode `>=2.2.3 <2.3.0`, tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5 and 2.2.6.
- In Jelly, the `access` setting is drawn as a choice of three, which needs a Jelly that reads declared choices: an
  older Jelly refuses the plugin's whole declaration.
- Updates are not automatic for a Git install, and `opencode plugin update` and `opencode plugin check` do not work on one: to move to a newer release, remove the old entry and add the new tag.

## [0.0.1] - 2026-11-12 The tool contract moves from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0 (`CONTRACT_VERSION`); the change is additive. Every 1.0.0 call keeps its meaning, apart from the refusals under Security and Fixed that correct defects, and new warnings. The chart document introduced here is version 1. ### Security - **Interactive HTML could run script from an ECharts tooltip.** In 0.0.0, and in the npm releases 0.0.2 and 0.0.3 before it, the page's CSP allowed `'unsafe-inline'` scripts, and ECharts writes a tooltip formatter string into the page as HTML, so a formatter such as `` in an option (the option can come from data or a model) ran its handler when the tooltip opened. Three layers now stop it: the page's `script-src` is the SHA-256 hashes of exactly its own two scripts (with `base-uri`, `form-action` and `object-src` `'none'`), so no inline handler, `javascript:` URL or injected script runs; every ECharts tooltip in an option is checked against an allow-list of attribute-free tags (`
`, ``, ``, ``…), and anything else, an attribute, a comment or an encoded `<` is refused with `ECHARTS_MARKUP_REFUSED` at its JSON path; and the same check runs inside the page before ECharts starts, so an edited page fails to its static chart rather than inserting markup. `{b}
{c}` still draws two lines. Regenerate any interactive HTML made with 0.0.0, 0.0.2 or 0.0.3 from untrusted options. ### Added - **Chart documents** (`ChartDocumentV1`, version 1): a typed recipe or a raw engine spec, its data, and its appearance, layout and interactions, checked strictly with a JSON path for every problem. `charts_quick` takes `document` (the recommended path for the 14 standard types); `charts_render` and `charts_validate` take `document` or a saved `documentPath` (with an optional `expectedRevision`); `document` is a new output format. A call takes exactly one input arm (`INPUT_CONFLICT` otherwise). See `docs/documents.md`. - **14 typed recipes** (`bar`, `horizontal_bar`, `grouped_bar`, `stacked_bar`, `line`, `area`, `stacked_area`, `scatter`, `bubble`, `pie`, `donut`, `histogram`, `box_plot`, `heatmap`) from one registry that owns each recipe's schemas, compiler, examples, data requirements and interaction and layout support. Aggregation is explicit: repeated groups without `options.aggregate` are `AGGREGATION_REQUIRED`, `count` counts rows and takes no measure, and a missing measure is left out and reported (`VALUE_MISSING`), never read as zero. - **The saved artifact** `.chart.json` (`opencode-charts-artifact`, version 1): the canonical document with its rows captured before the transform, the captured theme base, defaults, custom-font digests and colour domain, and a `sha256:` revision. Replaying it uses what it captured, not today's defaults. A result also carries a render `fingerprint`, and never the captured rows. - **`charts_update`**: a presentation patch (title, alt text, theme and token overrides, category colours, layout, interactions) to a saved artifact at a known revision, published as a new immutable generation. Data, bindings, aggregation, sorting, transforms, locale, currency and seed cannot change. A stale or edited revision is `DOCUMENT_REVISION_MISMATCH`, and a custom font whose bytes changed is `DOCUMENT_DEPENDENCY_CHANGED`, before anything is drawn. It is an `export` tool on every surface: registration, tools RPC, Jelly (`ask`), permissions and `docs/tool-parity.md`. - **Immutable generations**: a document call's files are staged whole and published as one folder `/-/` named by its file manifest; an identical existing folder is verified and reused, a different one is refused, and a failure publishes nothing. - **Recipe layout**: `width` and `height` are the outer canvas, exact in SVG and in PNG pixels × scale. Five targets (`inline` 720 × 420 responsive, `analysis` and `report` 900 × 540, `presentation` 1280 ×

## [0.0.0] - 2026-11-10

### Added

- **One tool registry** (`src/registry.ts`): each tool is defined once, and the plugin's tool registration, the Jelly
  declaration, the tools RPC, `charts_capabilities` and `docs/tool-parity.md` are projections of it.
  `test/registry.test.ts` fails when they drift.
- **`charts_capabilities`**: exactly what this build can do, computed rather than promised — working output formats,
  engines and the families each draws, themes and their palette sizes, bundled fonts and the scripts they cover, data
  formats, locales, atlases, limits, every tool with its class, and what is known not to work.
- **`charts_recommend`**: which chart fits a question, its data and its medium. A deterministic local ranking over the
  53-type catalogue with a reason for each pick, the encoding to use, and a ready `charts_render` call on the caller's
  own columns. It abstains with a reason rather than guessing, and it never renders.
- **The figure tree**: `charts_render` and `charts_validate` return the drawing as text — every label with a stable id,
  its box, and which labels collide or run past the edge — and the preview PNG numbers the same ids (`marks`).
- **The tools RPC v2** at `charts.tools`: every tool is a method with its class, so a script draws or checks a chart
  with no model. `docs/scripting.md` has the classes, the rule that decides a call and the saved-approval note.
- `FONT_GLYPH_MISSING`: a label using a code point no bundled face draws is named, with the characters and the fix,
  instead of silently becoming a blank box.
- `docs/tool-parity.md`, `docs/status.md`.
- **One typed code table**: `ChartsCode` in `src/errors.ts` is every failure and every issue code the plugin can
  return, and the README's and `docs/configuration.md`'s error tables now list them all — the validation and lint
  issue codes included. `test/codes.test.ts` fails when a code is raised that is not in the table, or either table
  differs from it.
- The tools `charts_render`, `charts_quick`, `charts_validate`, `charts_catalogue`, `charts_themes` and `charts_theme_save`.
- Engines: Vega-Lite and Vega (rendered in a worker with time and memory limits) and ECharts server-side SVG. PNG through resvg (wasm). Offline interactive HTML.
- Validation with did-you-mean and JSON paths; lint; layout checks (label collisions, clipping, duplicate ticks); PNG previews for the model.
- A cookbook skill generated from the 53-type catalogue.
- Bundled fonts: Inter and JetBrains Mono.

### Fixed

- Every tool declares its output schema, and it is a real one: the registry's, projected to the model path and to the
  tools RPC, which validates each script's result against it. This keeps 0.0.3's fix — OpenCode 2.2.5 fails a result
  from a tool that declares no output — and makes the declaration checkable, with no `pattern` (the shared module's
  rule for an owned output schema). A host case on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5 and 2.2.6 calls all eight tools and asserts every
  result is accepted.

- The TUI part (`dist/tui.js`) loads from a local-path install again. It is built unminified: OpenCode could not resolve the minified form of its `solid-js` import, so the status dialog never started. The build fails if the file is minified.

### Changed

- The Code Mode catalogue no longer pins `charts_quick` or `charts_render`. Their signatures are large; the charts skill holds the workflow, and `search({ namespace: "charts", query })` finds a tool.

- **Every tool is allowed by default.** The plugin inserts one `allow` rule for `charts_*` and one for each of the
  eight tools after every agent's base rule, so a render writes chart files into the workspace and a theme is saved
  with no prompt, and a tool a later release adds runs at once. An agent's own rules, your `permissions` and a saved
  approval still win.
- **The `access` option** restricts that in one line: `"all"` (the default), `"ask-changes"` (the five reads run, the
  three writers ask) and `"read-only"`
